verses.gurmukhi: ਜਉ ਪੈ ਤੰੂਬਰੀ ਨਾ ਬੂਡੈ ਸਰਿਤਾ ਪਰਵਾਹ ਬਿਖੈ ਬਿਖਮੈ ਤਊ ਨ ਤਜਤ ਹੈ ਮਨ ਤੇ ॥
verses.translit_en: jau pai ta(n)oobaree naa booddai saritaa paravaeh bikhai bikhamai tuoo na tajat hai man te ||

en.bdb: If a colocynth (Tumna) does not sink in fast flowing river and it does not shed its bitterness even in sweet cold water, then what good it is?

verses.gurmukhi: ਜਉ ਪੈ ਲਪਟੈ ਪਾਖਾਨ ਪਾਵਕ ਜਰੈ ਸੂਤ੍ਰ ਜਲ ਮੈ ਲੈ ਬੋਰਤਿ ਰਿਦੈ ਕਠੋਰਪਨ ਤੇ ॥
verses.translit_en: jau pai lapaTai paakhaan paavak jarai sootr jal mai lai borat ridhai kaThorapan te ||

en.bdb: If the flame of fire cannot burn the stone, and if due to its rigid nature sinks everything along with it, then what good it is ?

verses.gurmukhi: ਜਉ ਪੈ ਗੁਡੀ ਉਡੀ ਦੇਖੀਅਤ ਹੈ ਅਕਾਸਚਾਰੀ ਬਰਖਤ ਮੇਂਹ ਬਾਚੀਐ ਨ ਬਾਲਕਨ ਤੇ ॥
verses.translit_en: jau pai guddee uddee dhekheeat hai akaasachaaree barakhat me(n)h baacheeaai na baalakan te ||

en.bdb: A kite is seen flying in the sky like a bird, but when it starts raining it cannot be saved and retrieved by the children flying it.

verses.gurmukhi: ਤੈਸੇ ਰਿਧਿ ਸਿਧਿ ਭਾਉ ਦੁਤੀਆ ਤ੍ਰਿਗੁਨ ਖੇਲ ਗੁਰਮੁਖ ਸੁਖ ਫਲ ਨਾਹਿ ਕ੍ਰਿਤਘਨ ਤੇ ॥੪੭੮॥
verses.translit_en: taise ridh sidh bhaau dhuteeaa tiragun khel gurmukh sukh fal naeh kirataghan te ||478||

en.bdb: Similarly, acquiring miraculous powers is a sign of duality and influence of the three trait mammon (maya). A true disciple of the Guru knows that one cannot obtain virtues and comforts from this duality and betrayal of the Guru. (478)
